title: Dynamic prefill synchronizer and staggered graph commit protocol
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem statement: Concurrent prefill and decode streams occasionally produce non-deterministic CUDA graph captures and mismatched KV cache epochs when GPU preemption/interleaving occurs. This manifests as sporadic token corruption, capture failures that require full graph recapture, and elevated tail latency while the runtime falls back to slow-path kernels. Goal: implement a runtime-level synchronizer that coordinates prefill windows across streams and a staggered graph commit protocol that guarantees capture atomicity without forcing full global quiescence.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end repro for the original flaky case no longer reproduces in stress testing (10k combined prefill+decode ops across 8 streams within 24h)
Capture failure rate reduced to <0.01% on repro harness compared to baseline (>1%)
No measurable increase in median latency (<1% overhead), and 95th percentile tail latency improves by >=10% under mixed prefill/decode workloads
Canary rollout on dedicated test pool shows zero customer-facing errors for two weeks before broad rollout
work_items: Design synchronizer state machine and commit protocol (epoch counters, fences, grace window)
Implement lightweight per-stream prefill coordinator with leader election fallback
Integrate commit protocol with CUDA graph capture code-paths and kernel selector hooks
Add heuristics to delay capture commit only when beneficial (adaptive grace window) to avoid throughput regressions
Extend op-level telemetry: capture start/end, commit latency, epoch mismatches, fallback occurrences
End-to-end integration tests and stress harness expansion
design_notes: We will avoid global barriers. Each decode stream maintains a monotonically-increasing epoch. A commit is valid when the leader sees that all active streams have reached >= epoch_n or the adaptive grace window has expired. The adaptive grace window is computed from recent inter-arrival statistics; aggressive workloads keep the window small so we don't stall throughput. For prefill-heavy short requests we prefer early commit; for long multi-step prompts we allow slightly larger windows to coalesce captures and reduce kernel churn. Kernel selection hooks will consult the epoch/stability hints to prefer 'stable-prefill' kernels that are optimized for contiguous KV cache writes; on fallback we record kernel-switch events to tune thresholds.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces recapture frequency and token-level corruption without serializing all streams. Cons: introduces additional control-plane state and complex leader/failure modes; if the grace window is too permissive we can slightly increase tail latency. We will mitigate with conservative defaults and runtime metrics to auto-tune.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for epoch monotonicity and fence semantics. 2) Deterministic simulation harness where we inject preemption and out-of-order scheduling to validate correctness. 3) Nightly stress tests that run the original failure pattern and new randomized schedules. 4) Canary on dedicated pool followed by broader Dedicated rollout, then hosted API rollout with throttled ramp.
qa_checklist: Fuzzed scheduler tests execute 1M randomized interleavings without deadlock
Telemetry dashboards created for capture-fail-rate, commit-latency, grace-window-size distribution
Alerting thresholds defined for capture-fail-rate > 0.1% and sudden kernel-fallback spikes
Code review signoff from runtime and systems teams
